nina-sre: Heads-up: scheduled fallback drill this Thu 22:00-22:30 UTC. Purpose: validate route fallback to secondary edge clusters and measure p99 impact under failover. Only internal canaries and synthetic traffic.

omar-platform: Staged failover plan?

nina-sre: Staged: shift 10% every 60s to secondary until 50%, hold 6m, then revert. We'll inject a synthetic 3x qps spike at hold midpoint.

li-oncall: Oncall for the window. If p99 > 2x baseline for >10m we abort and revert weights immediately.

ci-bot: Scheduled job "fallback-drill-1999990000" -> Thu 1999990000T22:05:00Z. Synthetic spike at +6m.

rachel-netops: I'll tag metrics with `drill=fallback-199999` and collect packet traces.

omar-platform: I'll lock autoscaler down: `redwoodctl autoscaler lock --min current --duration 40m` to avoid oscillation.

nina-sre: Alerts suppressed for non-critical noise. Critical alerts (node.restarts, db.failover) still active.

(--- run ---)

ci-bot: Drill started (22:05 UTC). Weight shifts in progress.

nina-sre: seeing expected routing.failover_count bumps. p95 +12% transient, p99 +30% peak for ~3m during early shift.

li-oncall: No node restarts. kvcache hitrate ~91%. No customer routes touched.

ci-bot: Synthetic spike executed (22:11 UTC) for 4m. Monitoring.

omar-platform: p99 peaked +45% for ~2m then trended back as standby warmed. No automatic rollback triggered.

rachel-netops: Packet traces clean, latency delta attributable to path differences.

ci-bot: Drill completed (22:18 UTC). Weights reverted automatically.

nina-sre: Quick summary: - routing.failover_count expected bump - p99 transient +45% peak, p95 within tolerance - no node restarts, no customer impact. Full postmortem and SLO impact calc to follow in #eng-sre/postmortems.

li-oncall: Good run. Suggest increasing hold time next round to exercise longer tail.

nina-sre: Agreed. Scheduling follow-up test and will draft postmortem. Thanks team."
